answers.answer:
No. SCOPe does not treat these three groups as one homologous superfamily. In SCOPe 2.08 they are three separate superfamilies. All three sit under one fold, f.21 "Heme-binding four-helical bundle" (sunid 81344), in class f (membrane and cell-surface proteins). The superfamilies are f.21.1 Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes (sunid 81342), f.21.2 Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits (sunid 81343), and f.21.3 Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain (sunid 103501). In SCOPe the fold level groups proteins by shared architecture and topology. It does not claim common ancestry. Superfamily is the level that asserts probable homology, usually based on structural and functional evidence even when sequence similarity is low. Placing the three in separate superfamilies under one fold means the shared four-helix heme-binding bundle is recognized as a structural similarity, but SCOPe has not accepted it as evidence of common descent. It may reflect convergence or a limited, unproven relationship. The groups are:
- f.21.1 has families f.21.1.1 (formate dehydrogenase N cytochrome gamma subunit), f.21.1.2 (cytochrome b of the bc1 complex, including cytochrome b6 of b6f), and f.21.1.0 (automated matches).
- f.21.2 has families f.21.2.1 (FrdC) and f.21.2.2 (SdhC/FrdC and SdhD/FrdD transmembrane subunits, including CybL and CybS).
- f.21.3 has the single family f.21.3.1 (nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain).
Limits on use: a shared fold does not justify transferring function, heme stoichiometry, quinone-binding or redox-partner roles, or homology-based claims between these groups. Do not use one superfamily's structure as a homology-modelling template for another on fold similarity alone. Without sequence or profile support, a model would be a fold-level analogy only. Within each superfamily, homology-based inference is more reasonable, but it is strongest at the family level. For example, cytochrome b of bc1 and the formate dehydrogenase gamma subunit share f.21.1 but are different families. Any claim of a deeper relationship across f.21.1, f.21.2 and f.21.3 would need independent evidence, such as sequence profiles, conserved heme ligand geometry or phylogenetics. SCOPe's fold-level grouping alone does not supply that evidence.
